amendments.body: `snapshot_response_json()` only backfills legacy aliases for TAN/NH3/NO2/NO3/PO4/TDS/conductivity in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:86-96`, but `TankSnapshot` also renamed `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_l` to `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_c_per_l` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:20-21`. As a result, `/snapshot`, `/time/step`, `/load`, and scenario-load responses no longer contain the old DIC key, so pre-rename API clients that deserialize the old snapshot shape will fail even though the other renamed fields were kept backward-compatible. Add the missing top-level `dissolved_inorganic_carbon_mg_l` alias and include it in `legacy_chemistry_aliases`.
amendments.rationale: This is a real compatibility regression in the new response shim. The bead explicitly called out backward compatibility for API consumers, and the current alias set is incomplete for one of the renamed chemistry fields.

amendments.body: `OMITTED_TDS_CONTRIBUTORS` in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:9-12` says the 7-ion estimate omits "untracked nitrogen and phosphorus ions". That is false for this model: TAN/NH3, nitrite, nitrate, and phosphate are tracked and surfaced in the same response; they are merely excluded from the TDS/conductivity proxy. Reword this metadata to say those tracked species are omitted from the estimate, otherwise the new self-description still misstates model scope and can mislead users about what the simulation actually tracks.
amendments.rationale: The whole point of this change is to make chemistry semantics explicit. Shipping incorrect scope metadata undermines that goal and tells API consumers the wrong thing about the model.

amendments.body: `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/chemistry.rs:51-59` and `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/overview.rs:49-58` stop at `Est. TDS (7-ion)` / `Est. conductivity`, but never tell the TUI user which seven ions are counted or that nitrate/phosphate/organics are excluded. The API now carries that scope metadata, so the UI portion of this bead is still incomplete: a TUI user cannot actually tell what the estimate includes or omits, which was part of the acceptance criteria for the chemistry-semantics change.
amendments.rationale: This is a user-facing correctness gap, not a cosmetic nit. The bead’s deliverable explicitly required the surfaced TUI/API chemistry metrics to explain what is tracked and what important contributors are still omitted.

payload.summary: Reviewed the chemistry-semantics/TDS-labeling changes, read the updated snapshot and TUI files end-to-end, and ran `cargo test -p tank_api` successfully. I found three issues: the backward-compat snapshot shim is missing the legacy DIC alias, the new TDS scope metadata incorrectly calls tracked nitrogen/phosphorus species "untracked", and the TUI still does not surface which contributors the 7-ion estimate omits.
